name: Dollar Sign
tldr: 💲 marks money, prices, and costs, usually when someone wants an amount to stand out.

contextMeanings.meaning: It highlights a dollar amount or refers directly to money.
It emphasizes that a price is absurd, painful, or worth complaining about.
It can underline a cost while hinting that the amount is unwelcome or unreasonable.
It marks a budget, quote, expense, or other figure in a professional conversation.

platformNotes.note: In a direct text, 💲 commonly closes a casual sentence about paying, charging, or splitting a bill. It makes the amount feel more noticeable without requiring a follow-up explanation.
In captions and comments, it can turn a price into the punchline, especially when someone is describing an expensive purchase. The visible dollar amount supplies the joke, while 💲 adds the reaction.

In comments about luxury purchases, absurd menus, or expensive travel, 💲 often functions as a quick complaint about the price. It points the viewer toward the number rather than adding a detailed opinion.
In workplace channels, it is clearest beside a budget, proposal, or invoice amount. A casual 💲 may seem pointed, so professional messages can state the figure plainly instead.

generationalNotes.note: Gen Z often uses it as a price reaction, with the emphasis landing on how expensive or ridiculous something is.
Millennials may use it when discussing bills, shared expenses, or a purchase that cost more than expected.
Gen X will usually read it literally as money or a dollar amount, especially in messages about invoices and household costs.

warnings.title: Paid or spent?
warnings.description: 💲 does not show money moving away, so it can be unclear whether someone paid, owes, or is charging you. In a serious payment conversation, name the direction of the transaction explicitly.

warnings.title: Joke mistaken for a demand
warnings.description: After an invoice or quote, a joking 💲 can sound like a passive-aggressive complaint. Use plain wording when the recipient needs a definite answer about payment.

seoDescription: What does 💲 mean? It marks money, prices, and costs, often closing a sentence about an expense or an amount that feels painfully high.

longForm.overview:
💲 is the heavy dollar sign, and its most common job is to close a sentence by putting money at the center of it. People attach it to prices, bills, deposits, quotes, and unexpected expenses: “that table is $80 💲,” “rent was $1,850 💲,” or “the invoice came to $900 💲.” Sometimes it simply identifies the dollar amount; sometimes it adds a little disbelief about how much something costs.

The emoji arrived in Unicode 6.0 in 2010 with 💰, 💵, 💸, and 💳, a group drawn for banking and finance apps. What distinguishes 💲 is its plain currency-symbol form. It does not show a bag of cash like 💰, a banknote like 💵, or money flying away like 💸. It also does not show the direction of a transaction, which can make “that cost me $40 💲” and “you owe me $40 💲” depend entirely on the words around it.

That makes 💲 more flexible than the neighboring money emoji but also easier to misread. It can underline a real charge, complain about an extravagant price, or close a sentence whose meaning was already clear. The symbol itself is not flirting, approving, or hostile; the sentence determines which of those it becomes.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
💲 usually appears at the end of a sentence rather than standing by itself. A text about rent, dinner, shopping, repairs, or a new quote gets a dollar sign after the total, making the number the final point. “Groceries were $112 💲” reports a cost, while “that rooftop brunch is $75 a person 💲” sounds like price shock.

It also works when people want to joke about an expensive purchase without writing a complaint. The number establishes the absurdity; the emoji frames it as a reaction. In a group chat, someone might send “the concert upgrade was $180 💲” to make everyone focus on the price. Because 💲 does not indicate whether money is incoming or outgoing, people usually add a verb such as “spent,” “paid,” or “cost” when the distinction matters.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Avoid 💲 when the amount needs to be unmistakable, especially in an invoice dispute, payment request, or contract discussion. A symbol that can be used for both paying and being paid may leave the direction of the money unclear, and a joking use can make a genuine disagreement sound sarcastic. Write the amount and transaction direction plainly there.

It can also feel overly casual in conversations with someone who may take money talk literally, including landlords, clients, or older relatives. A symbol attached to an alarming bill may sound like the sender is minimizing the problem. If the point is simply that the cost is high, a clear sentence such as “that was more expensive than I expected” is less likely to create friction than relying on 💲 alone.
longForm.howToReply:
Match the use by responding to the number. If someone says “that jacket was $240 💲,” you can answer “that is painful” or ask whether they are keeping it. For a shared expense, say directly whether you will split it and how: “I can send my half tonight.” That preserves the money focus without forcing the other person to guess your intention.

If 💲 lands after your own price, quote, or expense, clarify when it matters. “That includes everything” or “the $500 total is still the best option I found” answers the implied concern more usefully than another emoji. If the recipient used it jokingly and seems disappointed, acknowledge the price before discussing alternatives. The sign can turn a number into a reaction, but the reply should still make your actual position clear.

faqs.question: What does 💲 mean from a guy?
faqs.answer: It usually means he is drawing attention to a price, cost, or payment. It is not by itself a romantic sign, though a surrounding sentence about who is paying can change the context.

faqs.question: Is 💲 flirty?
faqs.answer: No. 💲 normally marks money, often with surprise or annoyance at the amount. A flirty message using it might be about treating someone to dinner, but the emoji is emphasizing the cost rather than the romance.

faqs.question: What does 💲 mean on TikTok?
faqs.answer: It often reacts to an expensive item, meal, trip, or purchase. In comments, it usually points out the price and adds disbelief, especially when the amount seems excessive.

faqs.question: Does 💲 mean money went away?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. The heavy dollar sign identifies money but does not show movement, so it can refer to money spent, money owed, or a price being quoted. Read the sentence around it.

conversationExamples.message: that dinner was $96 💲 want to split it?
conversationExamples.interpretation: He is noting the bill and directly asking whether to divide it. Reply with your preferred split or say you will cover it.

conversationExamples.message: the rooftop table is $75 per person 💲
conversationExamples.interpretation: He is reacting to an expensive menu and may be checking whether the group still wants to book it. Ask for the total bill or suggest somewhere cheaper.

conversationExamples.message: we can do it, but that changes the quote to $4,000 💲
conversationExamples.interpretation: He is clearly flagging the new cost rather than joking. Confirm the revised budget and what work is included before approving it.
He is sharing the expense and probably wants help processing the shock. Ask what repairs were needed before discussing who pays.
The emoji expresses disbelief at the mistake or the price. Respond with humor, then confirm whether the booking should be cancelled or kept.
